any: Yasaka Pagoda at the top of the stone street: five storeys, 46 metres, rebuilt in 1440. Every photograph of Kyoto has it in somewhere, and now mine does.
dusk: Dusk on Yasaka-dori. The pagoda goes dark against the sky and the street empties in ten minutes.

any: The Nio Gate of Kiyomizu-dera, vermilion at the top of the hill. After the climb through the lanes, it is the first thing that lets you stop.
From the Okunoin: the whole Main Hall on its pillars, the stage hanging over the trees, the city behind. This is the photograph everyone takes. I took it too.
On the stage of Kiyomizu. Hinoki boards, great pillars underneath and not a single nail, and about thirteen metres down to the treetops.
The South Gate of Yasaka Shrine in Gion. The proper way in, people here say, though most of us come by the gate on the main street.
The main hall of Yasaka Shrine, vermilion and white. Somebody is always ringing the bell and clapping twice.
